biocUniTools gets Bioconductor build results from the Bioconductor Build System
(BBS) and from R Universe, and compares them. This vignette uses the devel
books because there are only a few of them; every function also works for
`"release"` and the other package types.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(biocUniTools)
```

## Bioconductor branches and package types

`uni_for_bioc()` gives the Bioconductor version, R version, and universe for a
branch.

```{r}
bu <- uni_for_bioc("devel")
bu
```

Each package type has a different name in each system. `bioc_pkg_types()`
lists them; functions take the `type` column.

```{r}
bioc_pkg_types()
```

`bioc_manifest()` lists the packages of a type in a branch.

```{r}
books <- bioc_manifest("devel", "books")
books
```

## BBS results

`bbs_nodes()` lists the BBS build machines for a type.

```{r}
bbs_nodes("devel", "books")
```

`bbs_status()` returns one row per package from one build machine, by default
the one building on Linux x86_64. It has the version and commit the BBS built
and the result of each stage.

```{r}
bbs <- bbs_status("devel", "books")
bbs[, c("Package", "Version", "commit", "install", "build", "check")]
```

## R Universe results

`uni_jobs()` downloads R Universe data for a branch. Without `packages`, it
downloads the whole universe, which takes a few minutes; it can then be reused
for every type.

```{r}
jobs <- uni_jobs("devel", packages = books)
```

`uni_status()` returns one row per package of a type. `source_build` is the
`R CMD build` of the source package, which builds vignettes. `check` is the
`R CMD check` of the Linux x86_64 binary job.

```{r}
uni <- uni_status("devel", "books", jobs = jobs)
uni[, c("Package", "Version", "commit", "status", "source_build", "check",
        "bioccheck")]
```

## Comparing BBS and R Universe

`compare_builds()` joins both by package. It adds whether both systems built
the same commit and whether their results agree. Results are compared after
`normalize_result()`, which treats NOTE as OK and WARNING(S) the same.

```{r}
normalize_result(c("OK", "NOTE", "WARNINGS", "WARNING", "ERROR"))
```

```{r}
cmp <- compare_builds("devel", "books", bbs = bbs, uni = uni)
cmp[, c("Package", "where", "commit_match", "bbs_result", "uni_result",
        "result_match")]
```

For workflows, BBS does not run `R CMD check`, so `compare_builds()` compares
`R CMD build` on both instead.

`compare_summary()` counts the matches and differences.

```{r}
compare_summary(cmp)
```

## Reports

The BBS and R Universe report pages on the biocUniTools website are made from
this data. `write_comparisons()` saves a comparison for every branch and type
listed in a YAML configuration, and the report pages read the saved files:

```{r}
#| eval: false
write_comparisons("reports/config.yml")
```

`compare_table()`, `compare_header()`, `compare_bars()`, and
`compare_details()` make the parts of each page, so you can use them in your
own reports.

## Changing where data comes from

The locations of the Bioconductor manifest and the BBS reports can be changed
with options. `{git_branch}`, `{type}`, and `{version}` are filled in.

```{r}
#| eval: false
options(
    biocUniTools.manifest_url =
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bioc/manifest/{git_branch}/{type}.txt",
    biocUniTools.bbs_url =
        "https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/{version}/{type}-LATEST"
)
```
